title: Pet-Friendly Hotels in Greater Cincinnati (OH-KY-IN) | PetTripFinder
meta_description: Verified pet-friendly hotels across the Cincinnati tri-state metro -- Ohio, Northern Kentucky and southeastern Indiana -- with real pet fees and policies read from each hotel's own official website.
introductory_copy: Every listing links to a pet policy verified directly from the hotel's own official website.
_boundary_note: PTF-CINCINNATI-MARKET-FACTORY-001. Corrected mid-run from an Ohio-only boundary (Hamilton, Butler, Warren, Clermont, Brown) to the full tri-state Cincinnati, OH-KY-IN metropolitan market, adding Kentucky (Boone, Kenton, Campbell, Grant, Pendleton, Gallatin, Bracken) and Indiana (Dearborn, Franklin, Ohio) counties as IN-SCOPE Cincinnati authority, not spillover. market_id/market_slug/state_code stay 'cincinnati-oh'/'OH' for continuity with the columbus-oh/dayton-oh/cleveland-akron-canton-oh naming convention (the ptf-market/1.0 schema carries one state_code per market; the tri-state scope is expressed through corridor included_cities/included_postal_codes, which are not state-scoped). Middletown, Monroe, Lebanon and northern Butler/Warren County require boundary reconciliation against the committed Dayton census before any identity found there is admitted -- see cincinnati-dayton-boundary-review.json. Do not expand into Dayton's registered corridors or duplicate its coverage.

corridors.name: Downtown Cincinnati
corridors.title: Pet-Friendly Hotels in Downtown Cincinnati | PetTripFinder Cincinnati
corridors.meta_description: Verified pet-friendly hotels in Downtown Cincinnati, Ohio, with real pet fees and policies from each hotel's own website.
corridors.description: Hotels in the downtown riverfront core and adjacent near-downtown Ohio ZIPs.
corridors._included_cities_note: PTF-CINCINNATI-CENSUS-RECONCILIATION-001 removed "Cincinnati" from this corridor's city list. The mailing city "Cincinnati" spans roughly forty postal codes across Hamilton County, so a city-tier match placed twelve discovered hotels -- in Mariemont, Oakley, Norwood, Evanston, the West End, Bridgetown, Symmes Township and Sharonville -- inside Downtown Cincinnati. That is the same failure the Eastgate properties suffered before PTF-GEOGRAPHY-NORMALIZATION-001, arriving through the city tier instead of a hand placement. Downtown now matches on its six postal codes alone; a Cincinnati-addressed hotel in an unregistered ZIP is reported UNASSIGNED rather than placed wrongly. This changed no existing assignment: every corridor member has always matched on postal_code.
corridors._geography_expansion_note: PTF-CINCINNATI-GEOGRAPHY-EXPANSION-001 added ZIP 45225 (Camp Washington / West End). This corridor's own description is "the downtown riverfront core and adjacent near-downtown Ohio ZIPs"; 45225 borders 45214 and 45202, both already registered, and sits 3.2 miles from the market centre -- nearer than 45219 and 45220, which this corridor has always held. Added as a POSTAL CODE. The city tier stays empty: restoring "Cincinnati" is what pulled twelve outer-neighbourhood hotels into Downtown.

corridors.name: Midtown / Oakley / Mariemont
corridors.title: Pet-Friendly Hotels in Midtown, Oakley and Mariemont | PetTripFinder Cincinnati
corridors.meta_description: Verified pet-friendly hotels in Cincinnati's eastern near-city neighborhoods -- Midtown, Oakley, Rookwood, Norwood and Mariemont -- with real pet fees and policies from each hotel's own website.
corridors.description: Hotels in the eastern near-city arc between Xavier University and Mariemont, along Interstate 71 and Red Bank Road.
corridors._included_cities_note: Deliberately excludes "Cincinnati": it is the mailing city for every ZIP here and for roughly forty others, so a city-tier entry would re-open the over-capture this corridor exists to fix. Norwood, Mariemont and Fairfax are separately incorporated cities and match only themselves.
corridors._rationale: PTF-CINCINNATI-GEOGRAPHY-EXPANSION-001. Seven identities, 3.8 to 8.0 miles from the market centre, in a contiguous arc east and north-east of downtown. They were unassigned because no corridor covered any Hamilton County ZIP outside the six downtown ones; before the census rebuild the city tier had been placing them in Downtown Cincinnati. Three of the properties carry "Midtown" in their own names and one carries "Mariemont", which is where the corridor's name comes from.

corridors.name: West Cincinnati / Harrison

corridors.description: Hotels on the western side of Hamilton County and along Interstate 74 out to Harrison at the Indiana line.
corridors._publishing_note: Holds three identities against a minimum of five, so it is SUPPRESSED and produces no route, nav entry or sitemap entry. Its members are still assigned and their labels still render. The corridor is registered anyway because the entire western half of Hamilton County had no geography at all, which is why a Harrison hotel and a Bridgetown hotel had nowhere to go; the next discovery pass now has somewhere to put what it finds.
corridors._rationale: PTF-CINCINNATI-GEOGRAPHY-EXPANSION-001. Harrison sits 19.9 miles out on I-74 and Bridgetown 8.3 miles, one road apart. Harrison was NOT folded into Lawrenceburg/Aurora: that corridor is in Indiana, and proximity across a state line is not a market rationale.

corridors._rationale: PTF-CINCINNATI-GEOGRAPHY-EXPANSION-001. Eight identities, above the five-property minimum. Oxford is 31.1 miles from the market centre -- inside this market's own committed radius, which already reaches Georgetown in Brown County at 40.2 miles, Brookville, Indiana at 34.7 and Williamstown, Kentucky at 30.6 -- and inside the committed discovery bounding box. It is in Butler County, named IN-SCOPE by the market's boundary note, and it is a university-visit destination with its own demand rather than an overflow of downtown Cincinnati. The Butler County directory listing them is corroboration, not the reason.

_geography_expansion_note: PTF-CINCINNATI-GEOGRAPHY-EXPANSION-001 resolved the 26 identities the census rebuild left unassigned. Four postal codes were added to existing corridors, three corridors were created, and one identity stays unassigned on purpose. No corridor was created to eliminate a null: West Cincinnati / Harrison holds three properties and is suppressed below the publishing minimum, and the single Petersburg, Kentucky identity is a bed-and-breakfast already ruled OUT_OF_CURRENT_CATEGORY -- it generates no route, so a corridor drawn for it would exist only to make a number look tidy.
